papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies an additive singular-value correction. In 124M–500M LLaMA experiments, it lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss; the paper also reports clean-test gains under label noise.
papers.relevance: Direct match to spectral regularization, training for low-rank compressibility, and memorization under label noise.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA models with $124$M to $500$M parameters, spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
Regularization coefficients are calibrated in separate tuning runs using final clean-validation accuracy, independently at each noise level for MNIST and at 60 % 60\% noise for BERT.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Defines behavioral rate as compressed LoRA-adapter size needed to retain held-out fine-tuning gain. Rates vary across frozen base models; correction spectra rank rates within a receiver, and compression can recover performance after corrupted fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Connects spectra, functional compressibility, LoRA, and noisy supervision.

evidence.quote: the same datasets can require substantially different rates across frozen models, with their ordering changing across receivers.
On Qwen2.5-7B, for example, GSM8K accuracy falls from 77.6% to 23.7% after corrupted fine-tuning and returns to 82.9% after compression.

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: ORCA applies temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in LLM training, then releases it. The reported LLaMA, Qwen3, and MoE runs finish with lower validation loss than Muon, including a matched-target LLaMA 1.3B comparison at 60k versus 100k steps.
papers.relevance: Tests how spectral shaping changes training trajectories and quality across model scales.

evidence.quote: While the penalty is active, the effective rank of the weight matrix rises sharply above Muon’s, although ORCA initially has a higher validation loss.

The standard Muon run, using its original 100k-step settings, reached the same loss at 100k steps ( Figure 2(a) ). Therefore, ORCA used 40% fewer tokens to reach this target, a 1.66× token-efficiency gain.

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting low-rank gradient subspaces during LLM pretraining. At rank 32 on a 1B LLaMA C4 run, its reported perplexity is 29.14 versus 33.82 for GaLore and 19.92 for full-rank Adam; reported optimizer-state peak memory is 0.2487 GB versus GaLore’s 0.3385 GB.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses the quality, optimizer-memory, and speed tradeoffs of low-rank LLM training.

evidence.quote: at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: ZIP-SR and ZE-EDEN redesign 4-bit AdamW moment quantization. Across paired GPT- and Llama-style pretraining runs from 130M to 2.7B parameters, both reduce TorchAO 4-bit AdamW’s validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW; eligible persistent moments use 1.0625 rather than 8 bytes per parameter.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimizer-state compression and model-quality tradeoffs across scale.

evidence.quote: Both methods reduce TorchAO’s mean gap at every model size.

storing both AdamW moments requires 1.0625 1.0625 bytes per parameter on eligible tensors, compared with 8 8 bytes per parameter for FP32 moment storage, corresponding to a 7.53 × 7.53\times compression.

papers.title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization

papers.summary: Monarch-Muon applies matrix-aware optimization to structured factors. At fixed structure it improves reported pretraining loss over Monarch-AdamW; separate 6.89B-reference systems measurements report 52.94 versus 68.87 GB peak memory against dense Muon.
papers.relevance: Useful for the quality, memory, and speed tradeoff of structured, matrix-optimized pretraining.

evidence.quote: Monarch–Muon achieves lower final validation loss than Monarch–AdamW in all four structured comparisons (Table 1 ).
The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs in Appendix A.1 .

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: Adds an SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank penalty to LoRA fine-tuning. In mixed-domain rank sweeps on three models, the reported penalty lowers mean Wiki perplexity versus unpenalized LoRA at every tested rank of at least 16, with limited training-perplexity cost in most comparisons.
papers.relevance: Direct test of whether controlling adapter spectra improves language-model adaptation and retention.

evidence.quote: a penalty weight of λ = 0.01 \lambda=0.01 lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 16 relative to unpenalized LoRA.
Fuller spectral utilization need not improve every perplexity metric, so effective rank should be interpreted jointly with mixture fit and the held-out probes.

papers.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

papers.summary: Uses module-matched LoRA rank sweeps under label noise against dense fine-tuning of the same modules. In a Qwen2.5-7B experiment with 20% label noise, the reported LoRA test-NLL gap remains above dense at every measured rank, including parameter parity.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses LoRA rank, generalization, and memorization under noisy labels.

evidence.quote: we repeat the measurement on Qwen2.5-7B ( Qwen Team, 2024 ) over 5,000 5{,}000 AG News examples ( Zhang et al., 2015 ) with 20 % 20\% label noise, adapting the qkv projections of the last six blocks at twelve ranks up to d = 3584 d{=}3584 against dense fine-tuning of the same modules ( 3 3 shared seeds; Appendix C.3 ).
G G remains positive at every measured rank and in every seed, parity included.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: GDLoRA decomposes full gradients into LoRA-accessible tangent and complementary normal components, then updates base weights with the latter. On Llama-3-8B Math10K, the paper reports 70.01 average reasoning accuracy at 21.6 GB, versus 61.79 GB for full fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Connects LoRA optimization geometry to fine-tuning quality and total GPU-memory cost.

evidence.quote: GDLoRA achieves an average accuracy of 70.01 with 21.6 GB of memory, improving over LoRA by 2.50 percentage points while requiring only 1.2 GB (5.9%) additional memory.
Relative to FFT, GDLoRA reduces memory usage from 61.79 GB to 21.6 GB, a reduction of 65.0%, while trailing by 0.62 percentage points in accuracy.

papers.title: Beyond Low-Rank Parameterization: Narrowing the Gap Between LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning via Gradient Decomposition

papers.summary: Idea2Prior records discovery, identity checks, assessments, and ranking for auditable idea-to-paper retrieval. Its historical 30-query comparison reports Hit@5 of 53.3%, versus 43.3% and 36.7% for the two web-research baselines, with weaker performance on HARD queries.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval, ranking, and evidence tracking in the proposed research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: it preserves search queries, candidate identities, assessments, filtering reasons, PDF availability, and the final ranking.
The advantage is concentrated in EASY and MEDIUM; ChatGPT leads on HARD.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: These are reported paper results, not independently verified findings. Repository links or availability do not establish reproducibility.

Ori’s quoted memory figure is optimizer-state peak memory, not total peak GPU training memory. The 4-bit paper establishes persistent moment storage but the retrieved passages do not establish full-training-memory or throughput gains.
Monarch-Muon’s large-model systems measurements and complete quality runs are separate experiments; its 6.89B systems result should not be read as a 6.89B quality result.
GDLoRA’s retrieved passages do not quantify end-to-end runtime or full-gradient reconstruction overhead.
Idea2Prior’s comparison is historical and does not establish superiority on hard queries or against matched lexical and embedding baselines.
The selected list omits CORE and some theoretical LoRA and Muon papers to preserve the ten-paper bound and prioritize the profile’s stated research goals. X analysis was disabled.
